chains.title: Risk allele T creates a stronger forkhead site, increasing FOXA1 binding at the 16q12.1 TOX3 enhancer and raising TOX3 expression in luminal breast epithelium
chains.element: Intergenic/intronic enhancer at chr16:52.56 Mb within the TOX3/CASC16 risk interval, active in ER+ luminal cells
chains.cell_type: Luminal (ER+) mammary epithelial cells, modelled by MCF7

links.claim: The T (risk) allele improves the match to a forkhead (FOX) core motif, so FOXA1 binds the T allele more strongly than the C allele; within the forkhead specificity group FOXA1 is chosen because it is the dominant, highly expressed pioneer forkhead factor in ER+ luminal breast cells (MCF7) and occupies this locus in ChIP-seq, unlike FOXA2/FOXO/FOXP members.
The variant sits in a FOXA1/ER-bound distal enhancer that loops to the TOX3 promoter; stronger pioneer binding increases enhancer accessibility and activity on the risk haplotype.
Increased enhancer activity raises TOX3 expression (allele-specific expression favouring T has been reported at this locus).
The effect is restricted to luminal ER+ epithelium where FOXA1, GATA3 and ESR1 are co-expressed, consistent with the association being strongest for ER+ disease.
Altered TOX3 (a HMG-box chromatin protein) dosage changes luminal progenitor differentiation/survival programmes, modestly increasing ER+ breast cancer risk.

predictions: FOXA1 ChIP or ChIP-allelic imbalance in heterozygous ER+ cells shows preferential pulldown of the T allele
FOXA1 knockdown abolishes the allelic difference in reporter/CRISPRi assays
EMSA with MCF7 nuclear extract gives a T-preferring complex supershifted by anti-FOXA1
TOX3 is the gene whose expression tracks genotype in ER+ tissue
falsified_if: No allelic imbalance in FOXA1 ChIP-seq across heterozygotes
Allelic reporter difference persists after FOXA1 depletion

chains.title: Null: rs4784227 is not itself a TF-binding-altering causal variant
predictions: No reproducible allelic imbalance in any TF ChIP at the site
No allelic difference in reporter or base-edited isogenic lines
A different variant in tight LD on the 16q12.1 haplotype shows the allelic enhancer effect
falsified_if: Base-edited isogenic clones differing only at rs4784227 show reproducible TOX3 expression and TF-occupancy differences

chains.title: The variant alters a GATA3 site, with the risk allele increasing GATA3 occupancy and TOX3 enhancer output
chains.element: Same 16q12.1 enhancer, which carries clustered GATA/FOX motifs in luminal cells

links.claim: The T allele strengthens a GATA-like element; among GATA-group factors GATA3 is selected because it is the luminal-restricted GATA factor expressed in MCF7 and bound genome-wide with FOXA1/ESR1.
GATA3 co-binds the same enhancer and is required for its activity, so an allelic gain of GATA3 binding raises enhancer strength.
Enhancer activation increases TOX3 (and possibly neighbouring CASC16) transcription.
GATA3 expression is confined to luminal epithelium, matching the ER+-specific association.
Higher TOX3 perturbs luminal lineage control and raises ER+ breast cancer risk.

predictions: GATA3 ChIP shows allelic imbalance toward T while FOXA1 ChIP does not
GATA3 knockdown, not FOXA1 knockdown, removes the allelic reporter difference
Motif analysis scores the GATA change more strongly than the forkhead change
falsified_if: No GATA3 occupancy at the element
Allelic effect retained after GATA3 depletion

chains.title: The variant weakens a CTCF-anchored boundary/loop element, redistributing enhancer contacts within the 16q12.1 TAD
chains.element: CTCF/cohesin-bound insulator in the TOX3/CASC16 interval

links.claim: The C (non-risk) allele matches the CTCF core consensus better, so CTCF binds ref more strongly and binding is reduced on the risk haplotype.
Loss of CTCF occupancy weakens a loop anchor, allowing distal luminal enhancers to contact the TOX3 promoter more freely.
Re-wired contacts raise TOX3 expression on the risk allele without a local change in enhancer strength.
Although CTCF is ubiquitous, the consequence is only seen where the relevant luminal enhancers are active.
Dysregulated TOX3 dosage contributes to ER+ breast cancer susceptibility.

predictions: CTCF ChIP shows C-allele preference and a CTCF peak overlapping the variant
Reporter assays in episomal context show no allelic difference (effect is chromatin-contextual)
falsified_if: No CTCF peak at the variant in breast cells
Episomal/STARR reporter shows a clear allelic difference in the FOXA1-dependent direction

chains.title: Risk allele increases binding of an ETS factor (ELF/EHF family) at the element, acting on CASC16/TOX3

links.claim: The T allele could complete a GGAA ETS core; within the ETS epithelial group ELF3 is chosen as the epithelium-restricted member highly expressed in mammary luminal cells.
ELF3 binding activates the nearby epithelial enhancer.
The primary transcriptional output is the lncRNA CASC16 rather than TOX3.
ELF3 expression is epithelium-specific, so the effect is confined to mammary epithelium.
Altered CASC16 levels modulate TOX3 regulation in cis and breast cancer risk.

predictions: CASC16, not TOX3, is the eQTL target in breast tissue
falsified_if: No ETS motif match or ELF3 occupancy at the variant
TOX3 is the only genotype-associated transcript

next_experiment: EMSA with MCF7 nuclear extract on matched C and T probes with anti-FOXA1 and anti-GATA3 supershifts: cheap, fast, and it directly distinguishes a FOXA1-driven T-preferring complex (H1) from a GATA3-driven one (H2), while a complete absence of allelic binding difference would support the null.
